analysis.title: Danske Markets Investment Tracker: AI investment tracker, November 2026
key_insights: Danske's overall read is that the AI investment boom remains on track despite regulation worries and the recent market hiccups. Consensus lifted 2027 hyperscaler capex slightly. Danske calls 2027 a critical year, because AI lab revenues must keep rising while capex lifts funding needs in credit markets.

Hyperscaler capex consensus for 2027 is USD1.349tn, up from USD1.342tn a month ago, and implies +47% growth in 2027. Growth is expected to slow to 8.8% in 2028 and turn negative in 2029 and 2030. The 2030 estimate was cut from USD1.429tn to USD1.382tn. Total 2026-2030 capex is about USD6.5tn, or around 23% of 2025 US GDP.

Company guidance supports the 2026 capex run rate. Amazon expects about $220bn cash capex and 'meaningfully more' in 2027. Alphabet kept its $195-205bn 2026 guide and expects a significant increase in 2027. Meta narrowed its 2026 range to $135-145bn from $130-145bn.

Asian and US capex indicators remain strong. South Korea and Taiwan chip exports and Taiwan export orders keep rising, and US imports of AI components, data centre construction and capex orders are rising. Taiwan DRAM exports and Singapore AI-related exports show slower momentum, and manufacturing PMI new orders are moving sideways.

Industrial metals prices have lost momentum and copper broke its upward trend. Danske reads this as weaker overall manufacturing, possibly cooling in AI-related investment into November, though chip exports point to supply constraints or crowding out as the more likely cause.

News since the last update: Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang was ousted, which created uncertainty about the outlook. CoreWeave's strong earnings and higher revenue outlook relieved credit and equity markets. Anthropic's run-rate revenue reached about USD81bn in late October, from about USD71bn a month earlier.

Regulation is a new risk. Democratic governors took office in key datacentre states (Texas, Ohio, Georgia, Virginia), which hold close to 50% of planned datacentre investment over 3-4 years. They are calling for a moratorium on new approvals until stronger laws are in place. Danske expects little effect on 2027 because 75% of that investment is already approved and under way, but possible delay and higher cost from 2028, with no halt.

AI use is growing faster than forecast, led by agents. Google processes almost 32bn tokens a minute, over four times a year ago. Agents account for 76% of OpenRouter tokens in October. Growth comes mainly from existing users using AI more, not from new users.

Consumer AI adoption is stalling in breadth. The share of US adults using AI fell slightly for the first time in Q3, and AI assists only about 5% of work hours. Consumer spending has more than tripled to about USD40bn a year, and 14% of consumers paying USD100 or more a month account for 60% of spending.

Business adoption is slowing and concentrated. About one in four US firms uses AI. On Ramp, 57% of tech-forward firms pay for AI, but adoption growth has slowed to about one point a month. The top 1% of firms account for 80% of spending on OpenAI and Anthropic. Anthropic now leads OpenAI among paying firms and is the only one of the two still gaining share, while SpaceX AI is growing fastest.

Token prices are falling faster than usage is rising. Ramp firms' token use is up about 18-fold in a year while spending is up about 7-fold, and the price per token fell 21% in October alone. Nvidia says token prices have fallen nearly 60% since May. Cheaper Chinese models add to the price pressure.

Compute remains scarce. B300 GPU rents are almost 50% above early January and slightly below the October record. CoreWeave rents for older chips rose 30-50% in Q3, and 2022-generation Nvidia chips are being re-rented at up to twice their original price. This squeezes labs that pay more for compute while earning less per token, but it supports further data centre investment.

AI lab economics are tightening. Anthropic's annualised revenue was USD81bn at end-October, up from about USD9bn at end-2025. Anthropic plus OpenAI reported run rates sum to about USD130bn. Anthropic's compute costs rose to 58% of revenue in Q3 from 48% in Q2, and its prospectus expects growth to slow. Danske says the key watch item is whether revenue again grows faster than compute costs.

A METR study concludes Anthropic is likely improving model capabilities at about twice the rate of March 2024 to October 2025, with roughly 80% of the acceleration attributed to AI-assisted R&D and none to faster training-compute growth. Danske flags this as higher 'loss-of-control' risk through recursive self-improvement.

Model leadership is rotating. Claude Fable 5.2 (9 Nov) ranks #1 on the Artificial Analysis index at 65. GPT-6.2 Astra (17 Nov) is #2 at 62 and Gemini 4 Neon (18 Nov) is #3 at 61. The best Chinese open model (Kimi K3.1 Pro) scores 46 and Europe's best (Mistral Large 4) scores 26. Fable 5.2 carries a steep cost premium, while GPT-6.2 Sol versions offer the best value for money.

Bottlenecks: memory (HBM and DRAM) is worsening, with Micron and SK hynix pointing to a tighter 2027 than 2026. DRAM prices rose further while NAND prices fell, and analysts expect memory prices to peak in 2027/28. Advanced packaging at TSMC is unresolved. Power and grid connection is seen as the most critical constraint, with interconnection waits up to 5 years. Cooling is not yet binding, and construction and permitting are worsening.

Behind-the-meter power is accelerating for large data centres (typically above 100MW) to bypass grid queues, and Danske expects tighter post-election regulation to add to the trend. Memory price increases have also lifted Chinese export prices on electronics to the highest export price inflation since covid.

Equity view: the past month tested sentiment rather than fundamentals. An exceptional rotation out of IT, amplified by the Democratic midterm sweep, repriced AI equities sharply, with Nvidia down about 27% in a month. Earnings and fundamentals are as intact as a month ago, and Danske says the rotation happened without earnings or fundamentals playing any real part, so it sees the entry point as more attractive.

Valuations: global IT now trades below MSCI ACWI on 12M forward P/E, the widest discount since 1995. IT trades at about 14x against an 18.5x average since 2010. Semiconductors trade at less than half the multiple of software despite far stronger earnings growth. EM Asia is at its lowest P/E in 15 years. Nvidia is at about 11x and SK Hynix about 2.2x, while Palantir remains at about 64x.

IT earnings are expected to grow 95% in 2026, 49% in 2027 and 22% in 2028, against 38%, 18% and 14% for MSCI ACWI. IT estimate upgrades of more than 40% YTD equal roughly 4-5 years of normal earnings growth. Hardware and semiconductors lead growth and revisions, while software lags.

Q3 2026 earnings: all major semiconductor companies beat expectations, as did four of the big six hyperscalers, with Amazon and Alphabet a touch short. Market reactions were muted or negative: Nvidia -3%, Alphabet -13%, Meta -7%, Intel -29%, AMAT -4%. Micron (+3%) and SpaceX (+8%) rose. The S&P 500 blended Q3 revenue growth is 14.6% and earnings growth 29.9% at 92% of reports.

Cash flow is shifting from hyperscalers to chip suppliers. The big six hyperscalers are seen at about USD -170bn of FCF in 2026E, with consensus expecting a sharp recovery toward 2030. Semiconductors are seen generating more than USD400bn of FCF in 2026E. Micron's roughly 1500% revenue growth is about one sixth volume and five sixths pricing.

Anthropic IPO (Nasdaq: ANT, 19 Nov): priced at USD83, above the USD70-78 range, and about 7x oversubscribed. It raised USD81.3bn plus a USD26.0bn concurrent private placement. It opened at USD111.50 (+34.3%), hit USD114.99 intraday and closed at USD97.17 (+17.1%), which is 15.5% below the high. The valuation at the IPO price was USD1.51tn (USD1.75tn at close fully diluted). SpaceX is already listed, and OpenAI is expected to list in 2027 at about USD1.0-1.3tn.

Concentration risk: with SpaceX, Anthropic and OpenAI, the 'Mag 7' weight of 34.2% of the S&P 500 would rise to a 'Mag 10' weight of 38.5%. These companies are not yet in the index because of inclusion rules.

Credit: hyperscaler spreads have widened since the summer, but funding costs from spreads are up only about 0.5% and most issuers retain market access. Much of the rise in funding cost is from higher underlying Treasury rates. Oracle is the exception, with the biggest spread jump driven by credit spreads and not by rates.

Funding gaps for hyperscalers peak in 2027 and the debt share of the build-out is expected to rise to 50-60%. JPMorgan estimates USD650bn of investment grade debt is needed toward 2028. With USD350bn issued YTD, about USD300bn more is needed over 28 months. 2026 is on track for record hyperscaler IG issuance, and Danske sees limited crowding out of US Treasuries.
Data centre SPVs add hidden leverage, since hyperscalers lowered capex needs by signing long-term leases with SPVs. Risk-off sentiment has widened spreads on tradable IG and HY data centre SPV debt.

Neoclouds are the riskier part of the AI chain. CoreWeave spreads are trending near distressed levels (1000bp) and Danske would expect debt markets to be closed to it. Only convertibles exist for NBIS and IREN, and equity signals less distress there. Neocloud IPOs (Firmus, Nscale, Lambda) were postponed or cancelled, which Danske reads as waning IPO demand.

Danske's four scenarios for the next 3 years are boom accelerates, boom continues, warning signs emerge and AI bust. Its current gauge sits at a balanced equity perspective, and the report calls the distribution of risks and returns highly uneven.

sector_views.rationale: They lead 2026 earnings growth and upgrades, and semis trade at less than half the multiple of software. The sector is seen generating more than USD400bn of FCF in 2026E. Danske calls the rotation entry point more attractive.

Software has derated and lags semis and hardware on earnings growth. Valuations are 'solid but still lagging' and Palantir remains at about 64x forward P/E. Danske shows the software valuation premium rebounding after its late-2025 collapse.
Plans are still rising and the big six trade at about 12-24x forward P/E. FCF is negative at about USD -170bn in 2026E, funding needs peak in 2027, and neocloud credit (CoreWeave) shows distress.
IT trades at about 14x 12M forward earnings versus an 18.5x average since 2010 and below MSCI ACWI, the widest discount since 1995.

earnings_insights: Q3 2026 (LSEG, reported vs consensus, blended growth y/y): NVIDIA revenue +103% y/y with a 6% surprise and earnings +105% y/y with an 8% surprise. Market reaction -3%. Danske says NVIDIA guides Q4 sales up about 90% y/y.

Q3 2026 (LSEG): Micron revenue +379% y/y (6% surprise) and earnings +1018% y/y (6% surprise), with a +3% reaction. AMD revenue +45% (2% surprise) and earnings +76% (7% surprise), with a +1% reaction. AMAT revenue +53% (1% surprise) and earnings +92% (6% surprise), with a -4% reaction.
Q3 2026 (LSEG): Intel revenue +21% y/y (0% surprise) and earnings +165% y/y (31% surprise), but the shares reacted -29%. Broadcom revenue +94% and earnings +97%, with surprise not reported (n.r.).

Q3 2026 (LSEG): Alphabet revenue +25% y/y with a 0% surprise, earnings -13% y/y with an -11% surprise, and a -13% reaction. Amazon revenue +12% (0% surprise), earnings -2% y/y (-4% surprise), reaction -1%. Meta revenue +26% (2% surprise), earnings +2% (10% surprise), reaction -7%. Microsoft revenue +18% (2% surprise), earnings +18% (3% surprise), reaction 0%. Oracle revenue +30% (1% surprise), earnings +35% (10% surprise), reaction -2%. SpaceX revenue +161% (13% surprise), reaction +8%.

Q3 2026 medians: semis and equipment revenue +73% y/y with a 2% surprise, earnings +101% with a 7% surprise, and a -3% reaction. Hyperscalers and AI cloud revenue +25% with a 1% surprise, earnings +2% with a 7% surprise, and a -2% reaction.

Q3 2026 S&P 500 (LSEG, 92% reported): blended revenue growth is 14.6% and earnings growth 29.9% y/y. IT shows revenue +44.2% and earnings +73.9% y/y, and 88% of IT companies beat on earnings. 78% of S&P companies beat earnings and 66% beat revenue.

Consensus 2026E-2028E EPS growth (I/B/E/S): IT +95%, +49%, +22%. Energy +97%, -8%, -15%. MSCI ACWI +38%, +18%, +14%. Communication Services -4% in 2027E. 12M forward P/E for IT is 21x for 2026E, 14x for 2027E and 11x for 2028E.

Nvidia (CFO Colette Kress, interim CEO, Q3 FY2027 call, 17 Nov): token prices have fallen nearly 60% since May, accelerating token usage and demand for compute, so GPU rental prices are rising across generations.

AMD CEO Lisa Su (Q3 call, 3 Nov): demand is higher than supply. Amazon CEO Andy Jassy (29 Oct): an AI accelerator is installed about every 14 seconds and customers are consuming capacity almost as fast. TSMC CEO C.C. Wei (15 Oct): moving full speed to increase capacity and stepping up capex.

Anthropic S-1/A: price cuts tied to new model versions and contractual discounts lowered Q3 revenue growth by about USD600m q/q. Compute costs were 58% of revenue in Q3 against 48% in Q2. Anthropic quarterly revenue chart: Q3 2025 USD1.4bn rising to Q3 2026 USD17.0bn. OpenAI Q3 2026 USD10.0bn.
Micron's revenue surge is mainly price-driven: about 1/6 volume and about 5/6 pricing.

macro_indicators.reading: USD1.349tn, +47% y/y (up from USD1.342tn a month earlier)
macro_indicators.interpretation: Consensus keeps lifting 2027 spend after Q3 earnings. This supports demand for chips, memory, power and electrical equipment suppliers through 2027.
Growth peaks in 2027 and capex falls later in the decade, which is a risk for suppliers once the comparison base turns.
Scale of the build-out is larger than Germany's 2025 GDP, so funding and power constraints become macro-relevant.

macro_indicators.indicator: S&P 500 blended Q3 revenue growth y/y
macro_indicators.interpretation: Blended figure with 92% of companies reported. IT at 44.2% drives the strength.

macro_indicators.indicator: S&P 500 blended Q3 earnings growth y/y
macro_indicators.interpretation: Blended figure with 92% of companies reported. IT at 73.9% and Energy at 152.8% are the biggest contributors.
IT earnings are expected to nearly double in 2026 while multiples compress, so the valuation case rests on earnings delivery.
IT trades at a discount to MSCI ACWI, the widest since 1995, which Danske uses to argue against an expensive-tech bubble narrative.

macro_indicators.reading: metals index and copper lost momentum, growth rate in metals prices clearly lower
macro_indicators.interpretation: Points to weaker overall manufacturing and possibly cooling AI investment, though Korea and Taiwan chip exports remain strong.

risk_factors: Monetisation of AI remains the central uncertainty. Labs are loss-making, token prices are falling, and Anthropic's compute costs rose to 58% of revenue.
Political and regulatory risk: moratoria on new data centres in Texas, Ohio, Georgia and Virginia could delay and raise costs of capacity from 2028.
Funding risk: hyperscaler funding gaps peak in 2027, with the debt share rising to 50-60%. Credit markets are open but more restrictive, and neocloud credit (CoreWeave) is near distress.
Supply bottlenecks in memory, advanced packaging and power and grid connection could slow the build-out. Memory prices are also adding to global inflation pressure.

AI safety and loss-of-control risk: METR finds Anthropic's model development is accelerating through AI-assisted R&D, moving closer to recursive self-improvement. A severe incident could trigger strict regulation.
Market concentration: a 'Mag 10' weight of 38.5% in the S&P 500 once SpaceX, Anthropic and OpenAI are included.
Capex growth slows to 8.8% in 2028 and turns negative in 2029-2030, which is a risk for suppliers beyond the 3-year horizon.
IPO market fatigue: Neocloud IPOs (Firmus, Nscale, Lambda) were postponed or cancelled.
Leadership uncertainty at Nvidia after the CEO's ouster.
Price competition from low-priced Chinese models and cheaper new model versions squeezes lab revenue.
charts_described: Slide 67 plots Anthropic (ANT) on its first trading day: first trade at 11:48 at USD111.50 (+34.3%), intraday high USD114.99 at 11:49, low USD92.72 at 13:18 and close USD97.17 at 16:00, against an IPO price of USD83.
Slide 52 charts Micron revenue growth of about 1500% as roughly one sixth volume and five sixths pricing.
Slide 66 shows quarterly revenue: Anthropic USD1.4bn in Q3 2025 rising to USD17.0bn in Q3 2026, and OpenAI USD3.8bn rising to USD10.0bn.
Slide 22 charts Anthropic and OpenAI annualised revenue, with Anthropic at USD81bn at end-October 2026 and the two labs about equal in September on the same basis.
Slide 83 compares AI US datacentre capex as a share of GDP with the 1860 railway mania, 1996 internet and 1959 electric and telephone build-outs, with 2.55% and 5.87% labelled.
vol_and_positioning: Sector rotation out of IT was described as exceptional. Nvidia fell about 27% in a month and was the hardest hit, while Amazon was the most resilient at +11% YTD as midterms favoured existing capacity.
Market reactions to Q3 results were muted or negative despite beats. The median reaction was -3% for semis and equipment and -2% for hyperscalers and AI cloud, and the average was -6% and -3%.
AI takers (beneficiaries of AI capex) continue to outpace AI spenders in equity returns, while token expenditure and Nvidia have weakened.

Anthropic's first day: demand about 7x oversubscribed and first-day volume of 847m shares (SpaceX: 522m). Intraday high at USD114.99 (+38.5%) and low at USD92.72 (+11.7%) before the close at USD97.17, which is 15.5% below the high.

Credit spreads on hyperscalers have widened since the summer. Oracle has had the biggest jump and may have more difficulty accessing bond markets than last year. CoreWeave spreads are close to the distressed level of 1000bp.
Danske sees six hyperscalers accounting for 47% of the US equity market in terms of the combined 12M forward capex headline, with that capex at USD1.25tn.
geopolitical: US midterm elections: Democratic governors took office in key datacentre states (Texas, Ohio, Georgia, Virginia) and flipped six governor's offices (Alaska, Georgia, Iowa, Nevada, Ohio, Texas), with calls for a moratorium on new data centre approvals.
US export controls took Claude Fable 5 offline for 18 days, from 12 to 30 June, and cyber-capable model variants go only to vetted users.
Trump ordered federal agencies to stop using Anthropic on 27 Feb after the firm refused to allow mass domestic surveillance and fully autonomous weapons.
Trump and Xi discussed AI on 24 Sep, set up an AI dialogue on risks and agreed a hotline for warning of harmful incidents. Trump backed a voluntary AI safety accord on 29 Sep.

China said on 3 Nov that it plans broad AI safety standards covering the whole model life cycle. China plans RMB4tn (about USD600bn) of computing-network investment over the 2026-2030 Five-Year Plan, and US sanctions limit its access to advanced GPUs.
EU Cloud and AI Development Act (CADA) aims to triple EU data centre capacity in 5-7 years and cites over-reliance on non-EU cloud providers as a risk to digital autonomy.
Copper prices were more volatile after the Iran war but remain on an upward trend.
cross_bank_references: Goldman Sachs expects token use to roughly triple in 2026 and to rise 24-fold from 2026 to 2030, and expects Anthropic's revenue to exceed USD600bn in 2030.
JPMorgan estimates a total of USD650bn in investment grade debt will be needed toward 2028.
McKinsey projects global data centre capacity demand will more than double from 102 gigawatts in 2026 to 220 gigawatts in 2030, needing USD5.2tn of investment.
Morgan Stanley's funding mix estimate underlies the data centre SPV debt projection.

tension_points.bull_case: Hyperscaler capex plans are still rising, with 2027 at +47%. All major semis beat in Q3, IT earnings are expected to nearly double in 2026, and IT trades at about 14x forward earnings. Demand for compute still outgrows supply, and the Anthropic IPO was about 7x oversubscribed.
tension_points.bear_case: Monetisation is uncertain. Token prices are falling faster than spending, Anthropic's compute costs rose to 58% of revenue, hyperscaler FCF is negative at about USD -170bn in 2026E, and funding relies increasingly on debt markets that are becoming more restrictive. Market reactions to beats were muted or negative.
tension_points.what_invalidates: AI-lab monetisation disappointing, capex intentions weakening and negative earnings revisions across the AI equity universe (Danske's 'warning signs' scenario). Danske says 2027 revenue growth from labs is the test.

tension_points.theme: AI lab revenue versus compute cost
tension_points.bull_case: Anthropic's run rate rose from about USD9bn at end-2025 to USD81bn at end-October. Usage is rising 18-fold on Ramp, and Goldman expects Anthropic revenue above USD600bn in 2030.
tension_points.bear_case: Prices are falling, with Ramp price per token down 21% in October, and Chinese rivals are cheaper. Anthropic's costs grew faster than revenue in Q3, and its prospectus expects growth to slow.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Revenue not growing again faster than compute costs, which Danske calls the key thing to watch.

tension_points.bull_case: Debt markets remain open. Hyperscaler spreads are not at prohibitive levels, funding costs from spreads are up only about 0.5%, and large recent bond deals show access.
tension_points.bear_case: Funding gaps peak in 2027 with the debt share at 50-60%. Oracle's spreads jumped, CoreWeave spreads are near the 1000bp distressed level, and neocloud IPOs were postponed.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Hyperscaler spreads moving to levels that block bond access, or more neoclouds losing market access as CoreWeave has.

tension_points.bull_case: 75% of 2027 investment is already approved and under way, and governors mainly want a temporary moratorium, so Danske expects limited effect on 2027.
tension_points.bear_case: Texas, Ohio, Georgia and Virginia hold close to 50% of planned investment, and conditions on water and electricity could delay and raise the cost of capacity from 2028.

theme_stances.key_argument: The sell-off in AI equities came from rotation and politics, not weaker earnings, capex or demand, so valuations are more attractive.
theme_stances.evidence: the rotation has happened without earnings or fundamentals playing any real part

theme_stances.key_argument: Lab revenue is soaring, but falling prices and rising compute costs squeeze margins.
theme_stances.evidence: But prices are falling, and in Q3 costs grew faster than revenue.

theme_stances.key_argument: Debt markets are open but more restrictive, and funding needs peak in 2027, with the weakest credits in neoclouds.
theme_stances.evidence: Debt markets are open but becoming more restrictive
